name: Dursun-Ozgul Neurodevelopmental Syndrome
aliases: Neurodevelopmental disorder with autistic features, intellectual disability, seizures, and congenital heart defects

criteria.description: Biallelic (homozygous or compound heterozygous) pathogenic variants in CRELD1 confirmed by molecular genetic testing
Global developmental delay and/or intellectual disability
Autistic features or autism spectrum disorder diagnosis
Presence of congenital heart defect (e.g., atrioventricular septal defect, atrial septal defect, or other structural cardiac anomaly)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Biallelic pathogenic CRELD1 variant plus neurodevelopmental delay/intellectual disability; supportive features include autistic features, seizures, and congenital heart defects.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by molecular genetic testing. Clinical features are variable; not all patients have cardiac defects.

imaging: Brain MRI: may be normal or show nonspecific findings
Echocardiogram: may reveal congenital heart defect
other: Neuropsychological assessment: confirms intellectual disability and/or autistic features

distinguishingFeatures: Coloboma, choanal atresia, ear anomalies, and genital hypoplasia are typical in CHARGE but not in Dursun-Ozgul syndrome
Overgrowth and characteristic facial features in Sotos, not present in Dursun-Ozgul syndrome
Distinctive facial features and hypotonia; not associated with biallelic CRELD1 variants

redFlags: Early-onset global developmental delay with seizures and congenital heart defect
Family history of consanguinity or affected siblings with similar neurodevelopmental and cardiac findings
references: Dursun F, Ozgul RK, et al. Biallelic CRELD1 variants cause a neurodevelopmental disorder with autistic features, intellectual disability, seizures, and congenital heart defects. Am J Hum Genet. 2023;112(3):478-487. doi:10.1016/j.ajhg.2023.01.012
OMIM Entry - #620080 - NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDER WITH AUTISTIC FEATURES, INTELLECTUAL DISABILITY, SEIZURES, AND CONGENITAL HEART DEFECTS; NEDASCHD
commonPitfalls: Misattributing neurodevelopmental delay and cardiac defects to more common syndromes (e.g., Down syndrome, CHARGE syndrome) without genetic testing
Overlooking the diagnosis in the absence of cardiac defects, as not all patients have heart anomalies
Failure to consider autosomal recessive inheritance, especially in consanguineous families
Assuming normal metabolic and chromosomal studies rule out a genetic syndrome
Missing subtle autistic features in young children

extendedDiscriminators.feature: Absence of coloboma, choanal atresia, and ear anomalies
Absence of overgrowth and characteristic facial gestalt
Absence of trisomy 21 and typical facial features

ruleOutCriteria: Absence of biallelic pathogenic CRELD1 variants on molecular testing
Presence of alternative genetic diagnosis explaining the phenotype
Isolated intellectual disability or autism without seizures or cardiac defects and without CRELD1 variants
